recipes.name: Cindy's Jambalaya
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound smoked sausage (such as Conecuh©), cut into 1/4-inch thick slices
0.5 teaspoon Cajun seasoning, or to taste
1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with juice
1 pound peeled and deveined medium shrimp (30-40 per pound)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or large pot over medium heat. Stir in sausage and cook for 2 minutes. Add onion, bell pepper, and celery; season with salt and Cajun seasoning. Cook and stir until vegetables are soft, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in rice, then add tomatoes with juice, garlic, chicken broth, bay leaves, and thyme leaves. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.

Stir in shrimp and cook uncovered until shrimp turn pink and are no longer translucent in the center, about 10 minutes. Remove the pot from heat and let stand for 5 minutes. Discard bay leaves before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cindy's Jambalaya
raw_recipe.description: This easy jambalaya recipe features tender rice, smoked sausage, shrimp, onion, bell pepper, and celery. It's a basic recipe you can play around with!

review.reviewBody: I would like one thing. Saute the rice till it turns white. then add wet stuff. THis will make the rice grain for grain. I am from New Orleans and this is how i was taught. Other wise. Right on.

I can't believe I've been published again! This really is a fantastic recipe for such an easy one! Like I said in the little blurb, you can add just about anything you want, even leftover rotisserie chicken. It will be the best meal you've ever made!!! 6-9-24 Still making this every once in a while but it's my favorite recipe. Yum Yum! Making this again on 12-22-25, so yummy!

We thought this was fabulous! Gotta love the one pot supper - less dishes :) If you're adding shrimp, make sure rice is almost done before adding. I threw mine in too early and the overcooked the shrimp. Oh well - didn't ruin the dish. I will certainly be making this again - thanks for sharing!!
I followed the advice of Mike and sauteed the rice before adding the liquids. HUGE difference! The rice is perfect. I made mine with sausage and shrimp with some Old Bay Seasoning. It's great.
Very good. Put some chicken in it [with the sausage and shrimp], browned that with the sausage. Made a double batch so I don't have to cook tomorrow. can't wait for the left overs.

Okay, Miss Cindy, ya did it again. I used a can of RoTel (medium) tomatoes and this was "off the charts delicious". Didn't change anything else. We had guests and I made a copy of the recipe, at their request, for them to take home. Easy, quick, delicious, one pot, did I say delicious? I love your style!

Wow! This is SO good!! I bought a 10-ounce package of smoked sausage and just used all of it. I had Creole seasoning on hand, so I used that and just added extra since Creole isn't as spicy. I used brown jasmine rice, so I added a little extra broth and let it cook an additional 15 minutes before adding the shrimp. Both of my daughters devoured their servings as well and asked if I would make this again sometime. Thanks, Cindy, for yet another awesome recipe!!

I made this in a slow cooker and it turned out great. I didn't have any cajun spice, so I made some with paprika, onion powder, oregano, thyme, salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper. i ended up with 4 tsp and used all of it. My kids liked it as is, but my wife and I added some tabasco sauce and it was perfect.
Increased Cajun spice to 1-1/2 tsp and added 3/4 jalapeno minced finely. Just the right amount of "kick". DELICIOUS. This is a keeper. I doubled the recipe.

This recipe was really easy and delicious. Probably the best jambalaya I've ever had, and certainly the best I've ever made. I doubled the sausage and shrimp, so I added another can of tomatoes, which made it just "saucy" enough to my taste. I also added a red bell pepper along with the green bell pepper. You really can customize this to your liking and to what you have. Next time I will add okra.
We used a packet of Seeds of Change Brown Rice and Quinoa in place of rice and chicken broth, and we used chicken sausage. This was a huge success with our guests and so easy!

I love this recipe. I do add chicken seasoned with cajun seasoning. I also cook my rice separately in seasoned broth and tomatoe juice, and add it in the end or to individual servings. It keeps leftovers from getting mushy. And we love the leftovers.
I add extra sausage, red and green bell pepper. I small can of tomato sauce. I also add cayenne pepper and additional old bay cajun seasoning. It's great!
Followed closely but added extra garlic

Only changes I did was had a red pepper instead of a green so used it, and added jalapeño pepper that also needed to be used up. Made with 1 1/2 cups of rice and 3 cups of broth. We loved it! Easy one pot meal!
I’m shopping out of my freezer and needed to use up shrimp. Saw this recipe and thought well I have andouille sausage in the freezer also! This is amazing. Thank you!

Good recipe. I used hillshire farms Hot jalapeño smoked sausage and a touch more Cajun Seasoning. To save time I used frozen diced peppers and onions and frozen shrimp. Came out great . Will make again and try chipolte peppers for some more heat.

I have been using this recipe as the base for vegetarian jambalaya for over ten years and it’s always a huge hit. I skip the shrimp, sub Field Roast vegetarian sausage (any variety works but the apple sage is my favorite), sub vegetable broth, and add 1tsp liquid smoke. I also use brown rice and about 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning for extra spice. Delicious.
